title: Unbiased Delayed Feedback Label Correction for Conversion Rate Prediction

problem.claim: Delayed conversion behavior can cause incorrect labels in conversion rate prediction, especially when models are retrained on recent data.

gap.claim: Existing methods may fail to introduce correct information about false-negative samples under data sparsity and dynamic data distributions.

contributions.claim: The ULC framework uses an auxiliary model to correct labels for samples with observed negative feedback.
The label-corrected loss is theoretically shown to be an unbiased estimate of the oracle loss based on true labels.
The framework constructs artificial label-correction training data through counterfactual labeling and uses an embedding-based alternative training method to address partial training data.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Comparative experiments on public and private datasets reportedly show that the approach alleviates the delayed feedback problem.
The authors report that the approach consistently outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Conversion rate prediction is important for online applications, and industrial systems retrain on recent data to capture changing distributions.
Delayed conversion behavior causes incorrect labels, while existing methods may inadequately handle false negatives under sparse and dynamic data.
ULC corrects observed negative-feedback labels with an auxiliary model.
The corrected loss is theoretically unbiased; counterfactual labeling creates artificial training data, and embedding-based alternative training compensates for partial data.
Experiments on public and private datasets are reported to show effective mitigation and consistent improvement over prior state-of-the-art methods.

unknowns: No quantitative results, dataset names, baselines, or experimental settings are provided.
